# @ic-reactor/codegen — AI Quick Guide

Shared generation pipeline used by `@ic-reactor/cli` and
`@ic-reactor/vite-plugin`.

## Install

Most apps should install CLI or Vite plugin instead of this package directly.

```bash
pnpm add -D @ic-reactor/codegen
```

## Main Use Case

Use `runCanisterPipeline(...)` when you need programmatic generation in custom
tooling/automation.

## Generated File Model

- `index.generated.ts` is managed output
- `index.factories.generated.ts` is managed output, written only when the
  canister sets `factories: true`
- `index.ts` is a stable wrapper
- app-specific logic should live in wrappers or adjacent modules

## Generated Factories (`factories: true`)

One object per method, bound to the generated reactor, picked from the
method's annotation in the `.did`:

- `query`/`composite_query` with no arguments: `createQuery` → `<method>Query`
- `query`/`composite_query` with arguments: `createQueryFactory` →
  `<method>Query`, called with the args (`getUserQuery([id]).fetch()`)
- update or `oneway`: `createMutation` → `<method>Mutation`; never a query

`<method>` is camelCase (`get_message` → `getMessageQuery`). A leading digit
gets a `_` prefix; a name another method or `index.generated.ts` (the hooks)
already uses gets `_` appended, methods taking names in Candid's order.
`getFactoryExportNames(canisterName, methods)` returns the names.

Each call is annotated `/* @__PURE__ */`, so unused factories are tree-shaken
even through the wrapper's `export *`. They are module-scope, like the
generated reactor: client-only apps; on a server build the reactor per request.

```ts
import { getMessageQuery, setMessageMutation } from "./declarations/backend"

const { data } = getMessageQuery.useQuery()
setMessageMutation.useMutation({ invalidateQueries: [getMessageQuery.getQueryKey()] })
await setMessageMutation.execute(["hello"]) // outside React
```

Needs `target: "react"`; with `target: "core"` the config is rejected
(`CodegenConfigError`) before anything is written. Switching it off
removes the file. An `index.ts` the user edited is not rewritten; the run then
returns a `warnings` entry until it has
`export * from "./index.factories.generated"`. Do not hand-write
`createQuery`/`createMutation` modules that only restate a method name; set
`factories: true` and customize in `index.ts`, whose own exports take
precedence over `export *`.

## Validation

The pipeline validates the config before generating anything and throws
`CodegenConfigError`. The same checks are exported for callers that want to
validate first: `assertSafeCanisterConfig`, `assertSafeCanisterName`,
`assertSafeModuleSpecifier`, `assertContainedPath`, `assertOneOf`,
`resolveContainedOutDir`, and `resolveDeclarationsBaseName`, plus the constants
`CANISTER_NAME_PATTERN`, `REACTOR_CLASS_NAMES`, and `CODEGEN_TARGETS`.

## Generation Failure Modes

- `outDir` must resolve inside the project root
- canister names must match `CANISTER_NAME_PATTERN`
- a `.did` that compiles to a module with no `idlFactory` is rejected — there is
  no service to generate against
- each `outDir` carries a `.ic-reactor-owner` marker, so two canisters cannot
  write to the same directory. Without it both runs report success while the
  second replaces the first one's declarations.
- the marker records a canister name, so it cannot tell apart two entries with
  the same `name` and `outDir`. `findSharedOutDirs(entries, outDir,
  projectRoot)` finds those across every configured entry, and the CLI and the
  Vite plugin fail the later entry with `sharedOutDirMessage(...)`
